search_row.title: Hamilton's rule
search_row.statement: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.
search_row.math: \Delta \bar{p} > 0 \iff r b - c > 0, with r, b, c defined as regression coefficients (Queller form via the Price equation)

fields.dct:source: W. D. Hamilton (1964) The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I
fields.delphi:proposedTest: In a cooperative system (social insects, cooperatively breeding birds, microbes), estimate r from genotypes and b and c from fitness measurements, and test whether rb > c predicts which individuals help.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: in Hamilton's original derivation, additive fitness effects and weak selection; in the general form, b and c are partial regressions of fitness on the actor's and the partner's genotype. Formal status: proved; exact in the regression form (Gardner, West and Wild 2011). Critics argue that the general form is close to an identity with little predictive content (Nowak, Tarnita and Wilson 2010).
